message.content: In lions, one of the most well‑documented dominant traits is the **presence of a mane** in adult males. The gene(s) that control mane growth are expressed dominantly, meaning that a single copy of the allele is sufficient for a male lion to develop a full mane. Females do not develop a mane because they lack the Y‑linked gene that triggers mane growth, so the trait is effectively sex‑linked and dominant in males.
